      Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-cit-1_22-cv-00047 / USCOURTS-cit-1_22-cv-00047-0

      FAPD-AI: The U.S. Court of International Trade remanded the Department of Commerce's countervailing duty final determination on corrosion-resistant steel products from South Korea, finding that Commerce lacked sufficient explanation for departing from its established practice of not reexamining the countervailability of equity infusions absent new information. The court identified issues with Commerce's treatment of debt-to-equity restructurings and calculations of certain benchmark rates used to measure subsidy benefits. USCOURTS-SEL-02

    • Observed at 23:30:15 Eastern time ET

      FAPD-AI: The U.S. Court of International Trade remanded Commerce's redetermination, concluding that Commerce's explanation on remand did not adequately address the court's prior concerns regarding whether the first three debt-to-equity restructurings should be reexamined and how benefits from those restructurings passed through following a change in ownership.   • Observed at 23:09:31 Eastern time ET
    USA v. Eric Valentine (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca7-24-03222 / USCOURTS-ca7-24-03222-0

    FAPD-AI: Valentine appealed his bank robbery conviction, challenging dismissal of an earlier indictment without prejudice under the Speedy Trial Act and the denial of funding for a mitigation expert at sentencing. The Seventh Circuit affirmed both decisions, finding no abuse of discretion given the seriousness of the offense and the absence of government bad faith or defense prejudice, and finding Valentine's expert funding request lacked sufficient specificity. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 23:09:31 Eastern time ET
    Migdonio Altamirano v. Eric Emmerich (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca7-25-03197 / USCOURTS-ca7-25-03197-0

    FAPD-AI: Altamirano, a federal prisoner subject to a final removal order, petitioned for habeas corpus claiming earned-time credits entitled him to prerelease custody under the First Step Act. The Seventh Circuit affirmed denial of the petition, holding that 18 U.S.C. § 3632(d)(4)(E)(i) renders prisoners subject to final removal orders ineligible to apply time credits under the Act. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 23:09:31 Eastern time ET
    USA v. Kenneth Wright (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca7-26-01263 / USCOURTS-ca7-26-01263-0

    FAPD-AI: The Seventh Circuit affirmed the district court's revocation of Kenneth Wright's supervised release and imposed a 12-month sentence after Wright admitted to violating his release conditions by testing positive for THC. The appellate court found no non-frivolous arguments against the revocation or sentence. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 23:09:31 Eastern time ET
    Tam Ho v. Town of Whiteland, et al (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca7-26-01347 / USCOURTS-ca7-26-01347-0

    FAPD-AI: Tam Ho appealed a summary judgment dismissing her civil rights suit against town officials, arguing the district court displayed bias in its proceedings. The Seventh Circuit rejected Ho's allegations as insufficient to establish an appearance of impropriety and affirmed the summary judgment. USCOURTS-SEL-01

  • Observed at 23:09:31 Eastern time ET
    Demarcus J. Steward v. Eight Eleven Group LLC (opens in a new tab)
    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca7-26-01424 / USCOURTS-ca7-26-01424-0

    FAPD-AI: The Seventh Circuit reversed the district court's dismissal of Demarcus Steward's Title VII discrimination suit against Eight Eleven Group LLC, finding his allegations that the company prevented him from applying because of his race and sex stated a valid claim. The court held that Title VII does not require a formal application and applies a 'motivating factor' standard rather than a 'but-for cause' standard. USCOURTS-SEL-01

    Judicial opinion · govinfo API · USCOURTS-ca6-26-03059 / USCOURTS-ca6-26-03059-0

    FAPD-AI: The U.S. Court of Appeals for the Sixth Circuit reversed a district court's dismissal of Beverly Mowry's Federal Tort Claims Act wrongful death claim. The case involved a USPS truck that struck and severely injured David Mowry; the Mowrys had previously won a judgment for his personal injuries, but the district court dismissed Beverly's subsequent wrongful death suit as barred by res judicata.     FAPD-AI: Public Law 119-122, enacted October 15, 2026, amends the Crow Tribe Water Rights Settlement Act of 2010. The law restructures provisions related to municipal and rural infrastructure projects, repeals Section 406 of the original settlement act, and establishes an MR&I Projects Account within the Crow Settlement Fund. The legislation also extends the authorization period for Yellowtail Dam from 15 to 20 years and clarifies that the Crow Tribe retains title to and control over infrastructure constructed with settlement funds.     Airworthiness Directives; General Electric Company Engines (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · DEPARTMENT OF TRANSPORTATION · FR-2026-10-22 / 2026-21590

    official summary: The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain General Electric Company (GE) Model CF34-8C1, CF34-8C5, CF34-8C5A1, CF34-8C5A2, CF34-8C5B1, CF34-8E2, CF34-8E2A1, CF34-8E5, CF34-8E5A1, CF34-8E5A2, CF34-8E5A2HA, CF34-8E6, and CF34-8E6A1 engines. This AD was prompted by reports of in-flight “Engine Degraded” messages from the engine indicating and crew alerting system (EICAS) due to corrosion of the variable geometry (VG) system actuator. This AD requires removing certain electronic engine control (EEC) full authority digital electronic control (FADEC) software versions from service and installing an updated EEC FADEC software that is eligible for installation. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products. FR-SEL-01

    Utah Underground Injection Control Program; Class VI Primacy (opens in a new tab)
    Federal Register · govinfo API · ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY · FR-2026-10-22 / 2026-21618

    official summary: The U.S. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA or Agency) has received a complete Underground Injection Control (UIC) program revision application from the State of Utah, requesting primary enforcement responsibility (primacy) for Class VI injection wells under Safe Drinking Water Act (SDWA) section 1422. The EPA's approval of the State's UIC program revision application would allow the Utah Department of Natural Resources, Division of Oil, Gas and Mining (DOGM) to issue and enforce compliance with UIC Class VI permits for injection wells used for geologic carbon sequestration. In this action, the EPA proposes to approve Utah's application to implement the UIC program for Class VI injection wells located within the State, except those on Indian lands for which the EPA retains primacy. The EPA has determined that Utah's UIC Class VI program meets Federal requirements for primacy under SDWA section 1422 and the applicable implementing regulations in 40 CFR parts 144, 145, and 146.
